LESSON: WRITING 6.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING: POETRY

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.3: Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry, part of Strand 6 in Grade 6 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: when composing a poem, • compose simple poems and present to the class, • read a variety of poems. Why do we compose poems?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify stanza and rhythm in a poem for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. compose a poem for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. enjoy indigenous poetry for lifelong learning.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify stanza and rhythm in a poem for information,

   Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. compose a poem for comprehension,

   Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. enjoy indigenous poetry for lifelong learning.

   Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. identify aspects of poetry such as stanzas and rhythm,

2. team up to search for poems from online platforms and copy them,

3. work jointly to recite simple poems,

4. brainstorm on ideas incorporated

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. identify aspects of poetry such as stanzas and rhythm,
2. team up to search for poems from online platforms and copy them,
3. work jointly to recite simple poems,
4. brainstorm on ideas incorporated

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and Imagination: This is developed as the learner exchanges ideas that inspire creativity when composing

and reciting poems.

● Digital Literacy: This is enhanced as the learner interacts with technology when using digital devices to search for

poems online.

36

Values:
● Respect: This is enhanced as the learner takes into consideration the ideas presented by other members and

incorporates them when composing a poem.

● Integrity: This is promoted as the learner displays transparency when using technology to access information on

poems without visiting other sites.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Safety and security: This is developed as the learner interacts with the theme and composes different poems on health

and diseases and ways of keeping safe from diseases.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of poetry to their learning of creative works in Creative Arts.

37

income, teacher, pilot, doctor, farmer, artist, driver, lawyer
